evidence.snippet: City tour through San Telmo (in German) Discover with me San Telmo, the historic heart of Buenos Aires. We will visit the Parque Lezama, talk about the former Palacio Lezama, and the Museo Histórico Nacional. We also see the monument to Argentine-Uruguayan friendship and the monument to Pedro de Mendoza, the founder of the city. We then walk along Calle Defensa to Plaza Dorrego, known for its antiques and tango. We visit the colonial house \"Solar de French\" and the church Nuestra Señora de Belén, where I tell you about Pedro González Telmo - the patron saint of sailors and the namesake of the district. Finally, we will explore the Mercado de San Telmo with its special flair. The tour is in German - ideal for anyone who wants to experience history in a lively way!
evidence.title: City Tour Through San Telmo

evidence.snippet: Discover the colonial history of Buenos Aires and Argentina on a guided San Telmo walking tour. Explore the city's transformation from a small village to a cosmopolitan hub, with engaging stories about its foundation, native peoples, invasions, and independence. This experience is perfect for culture and history enthusiasts seeking a professional and modern approach. - Walk through San Telmo, the oldest neighborhood in Buenos Aires, and hear tales from the Colonial era. - Learn about local icons like Mafalda, the minimal house, and the Aborigines of Argentina. - Visit landmarks such as the San Telmo Market, the Ezeiza Mansion, and Lezama Park, which marks the foundation of the city. - Discover unique spots like San Lorenzo Passage, the apple of lights, and the Ex Eva Peron Foundation.
evidence.title: San Telmo Colonial Walking Tour – Buenos Aires History

evidence.snippet: Begin your journey through Buenos Aires’ history with a guided visit to Casa Mínima, the city’s narrowest house, tucked away behind a facade just 2.3 meters wide. This intimate space is a living relic of San Telmo, preserving the neighborhood’s oldest myths and traditions. As you step inside, you’ll discover how the house’s walls have witnessed the transformation from the era of slavery to the vibrant origins of tango, offering a rare glimpse into the lives that shaped this iconic district.Your guide will lead you through Casa Mínima and the adjacent corner space, revealing stories of freedom, resilience, and daily life in 19th-century Buenos Aires. Learn how a grand mansion was divided into a tenement, reflecting the changing fortunes and diverse communities of San Telmo. Marvel at the preserved original materials and archaeological finds that bring the neighborhood’s past to life, from hidden courtyards to artifacts unearthed during careful restoration.The tour concludes at the heart of San Telmo, leaving you perfectly placed to continue exploring the area’s lively streets, historic cafes, and vibrant markets at your own pace.
evidence.title: Buenos Aires: Casa Mínima Guided Tour in San Telmo
